subject: A change that invalidates earlier work has neither a plan nor a check
recordedOccasion: while resolving `0037` and finding its seven resolutions had been undone
severity: F1 is high — one commit reverted seven resolved findings and no instrument noticed, in the tree whose whole purpose is that work is not lost. F2 is the owner's standing preference with nothing behind it.
feltAt: the ten migrated bundles under 0037 D2
scope: session management. F1 wants a check, F2 wants a rule

members.statement: Nothing re-verifies that a resolution still holds, and one refactor reverted seven without anything noticing
members.sectionHeading: F1 — a resolution is written once and never checked again

resolution.whatWasDone: `bin/verify-doc-paths.sh` moves its historical branch below the resolution fallbacks and renames the count `DECAYED`; 36 decayed citations across 271 documents, six relocations accounting for nearly all

members.statement: A breaking change to a record format has no migration-plan requirement, so what happens to what predates it is decided per change or not at all
members.sectionHeading: F2 — a breaking change has no migration plan

resolution.whatWasDone: `.github/session-management-instructions.md` §6 gains the migration-plan gate: the conformance test, the five things a plan names, and one format change per revision

members.statement: Rolling a record file over to a fresh one is a format change that leaves every instrument reading the old path, and there is no rule requiring the readers to be named before the roll
members.sectionHeading: F3 — a rollover is a format change, and its readers are not named

resolution.whatWasDone: `bin/verify-manifest-coverage.sh` reads every `APPLY-MANIFEST*.md` rather than the current file, and the `git log` pathspec matches the set. Verified both directions: MISSING 0 against the tree, identical to the pre-rollover figures, and MISSING 1 with one archived entry removed

decisions.decision: A write that makes existing records non-conformant is gated on a migration plan as well as on the finding. The test is whether a checker would report existing records as failures, not whether the author calls it a format change. A plan names five things, and one format change goes per revision
decisions.sectionHeading: D1 — the gate, the test, and the five things

decisions.decision: The instrument is the resolver that already exists, corrected — `HISTORICAL` moves below the resolution fallbacks and becomes `DECAYED`, meaning cited by a record and no longer there. No second checker, and the reading half is declared irreducible rather than implied covered
decisions.sectionHeading: D2 — the signal was already being computed and half of it was mislabelled

decisions.decision: Coverage reads the manifest SET, `APPLY-MANIFEST*.md`, rather than the current file; and a rollover owes the same naming of readers that a format change owes of records
decisions.sectionHeading: D3 — read the set, and name the readers before the roll

edges.why: the migrated-bundle class is the instance F2 generalises

indexNotes: Recorded by `typed-bundles-architecture-20260908-204724`, which does not own it. F1 is the reading behind `0037`'s regression; F2 is the owner's retrofit preference, stated and unbacked
